scope: U.S. merchant business/product audit; direct merchant portal and merchant-services-provider/OptBlue routes distinguished. No technical/vendor architecture or implementation scoring.

field_semantics.normal_flow: Proposed Etail customer/business journey, not a claim that Amex exposes every step identically.
field_semantics.exceptions: Business conditions Etail must resolve or explicitly leave unsupported.
field_semantics.issuing_handoff: Proposed relationship to the payer/cardholder/issuer or Seller commercial spending; guests need no Etail account.
field_semantics.account_control_handoff: Proposed permission/responsibility boundaries consistent with Etail PRODUCT and WORKFLOWS.
field_semantics.evidence_status: Amex public business evidence: documented confirms the relevant task/observable behavior; partial leaves material program/exception detail unverified; gap lacks sufficient public U.S. evidence. Never an app-completion score.
field_semantics.source_ids: Contextual evidence for the relevant business task, not proof of every proposed acceptance clause. M IDs resolve in merchant-sources.json; N IDs in merchant-360-sources.json; B01 resolves in business-360-sources.json.
field_semantics.comparison_ids: Related rows of amex-public-v1, not an equivalence assertion. Empty means this business task is not a distinct existing comparison row.
field_semantics.etail_gap: Business specification or review gap. Application implementation was not inspected in this audit.
field_semantics.acceptance_scenario: Fictional proposed Etail acceptance scenario; amounts and outcomes are not Amex policies.

checks.journey: Choose the merchant program and responsible business
checks.normal_flow: Identify the legal Seller, operating country, permitted channels, fees, funding party and support route before offering acceptance.
checks.exceptions: Ineligible activity, unsupported country, a different business using the same login, or confusion between direct acceptance and OptBlue.
checks.issuing_handoff: A merchant approval does not open an issuing facility or guarantee a payer's card approval.
checks.account_control_handoff: An administrator cannot accept terms or change the responsible party without that authority.
checks.etail_gap: The current product needs an explicit program/responsibility explanation; real provider and negotiated terms remain unselected.
checks.acceptance_scenario: Given a fictional provider that only forwards transactions, the Seller sees the separate funder and dispute contact and cannot assume the forwarding provider pays it.

checks.journey: Apply, supply missing information and receive an activation outcome
checks.normal_flow: Start or resume the named Seller request, complete requirements, review responsibility, submit and receive pending, needs-information, approved or declined status.
checks.exceptions: Abandoned draft, missing requirement, repeated submission, unapproved representative or later restriction.
checks.issuing_handoff: Merchant activation and commercial spending approval remain separate customer decisions.
checks.account_control_handoff: Only the named representative may submit; a helper can assist only within delegated authority.
checks.etail_gap: Requirements exist; the complete business review and recovery journey has not been assessed in the application.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An applicant returns after a missing-information request, finishes the same application and receives one recorded outcome; the pending Seller cannot collect.

checks.journey: Set up locations and who receives their money
checks.normal_flow: Add approved locations; identify which location submits sales and whether funds go to a central or local payee.
checks.exceptions: Wrong parent, closed location, duplicate setup, one rejected item in several requests or a changed payee.
checks.issuing_handoff: The payer's receipt identifies the actual seller/location without revealing internal ownership details.
checks.account_control_handoff: Location oversight does not automatically give the manager access to another legal Seller.
checks.etail_gap: Multi-location business rules and per-item outcomes need a customer walkthrough; existing comparison rows cover only part of that journey.
checks.acceptance_scenario: One headquarters requests two locations; one succeeds and one requires correction. Central finance can distinguish the two and their separate destinations.

checks.journey: Give, review and remove merchant team access
checks.normal_flow: Give each person the required location and service access, show its scope, review users and remove access when duties end.
checks.exceptions: Departed staff, wrong location, bookkeeper attempting a refund, dispute responder attempting a bank change or old export access.
checks.issuing_handoff: Merchant staff receive only purchase/case information needed to service the sale, not the payer's unrelated card activity.
checks.account_control_handoff: Merchant administration, financial action, dispute response and reporting are separate permissions.
checks.etail_gap: The role model exists; end-to-end merchant role exercises and handoffs remain unassessed.
checks.acceptance_scenario: Remove a location manager while a dispute draft is open; another authorized responder can finish it, but the removed manager cannot read or submit it.

checks.journey: Make the seller, sale terms and receipt understandable
checks.normal_flow: Show who is selling, price/currency, cancellation/return conditions and a receipt/reference that lets buyer and Seller recognize the same sale.
checks.exceptions: Unrecognizable descriptor, wrong location, unclear fee, missing receipt or a buyer contacting the wrong business.
checks.issuing_handoff: The cardholder can connect the statement charge with the purchase and its service contact.
checks.account_control_handoff: Only authorized staff change customer-facing business details; changes are reviewed in the proper Seller.
checks.etail_gap: Receipt and public checkout requirements exist; consistent merchant identity from checkout to cardholder support needs a specific business review.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A buyer queries a fictional statement descriptor; the receipt identifies the seller and purchase without requiring access to a private merchant account.

checks.journey: Accept a payment and handle approval, decline or uncertainty
checks.normal_flow: Present the intended amount, obtain the supported payment decision and tell both sides whether payment is approved, declined, cancelled or still unknown.
checks.exceptions: Expired approval, attempted amount above approval, partial approval, buyer abandonment or an interrupted response.
checks.issuing_handoff: Issuer approval/rejection and the buyer's hold must match the merchant's payment status; neither side infers settlement from approval.
checks.account_control_handoff: A cashier cannot override a restriction or raise a spending limit; unsupported channels are disclosed.
checks.etail_gap: Acquiring is specified, but channel-specific customer recovery, partial-approval policy and responsibility for uncertain payments need explicit decisions.
checks.acceptance_scenario: The buyer sees a connection failure after approval; the Seller checks the existing payment before asking for another payment and the buyer is not charged twice.

checks.journey: Manage fulfillment, partial delivery and cancellation
checks.normal_flow: Record what was promised and delivered, keep the buyer informed, and collect or refund only the amount justified by the agreed sale and approved payment arrangement.
checks.exceptions: Delayed shipment, partial delivery, cancelled service, unfulfilled deposit or goods refused on delivery.
checks.issuing_handoff: Cardholder purchase/credit history reflects the fulfilled and cancelled portions separately.
checks.account_control_handoff: Staff can record fulfillment without gaining permission to change price, issue a refund or alter the underlying sale terms.
checks.etail_gap: Etail offers deposits and invoices; it still needs explicit advance-payment, partial-fulfillment and cancellation policies before those affected flows.
checks.acceptance_scenario: For a fictional 100-dollar order,60 dollars is fulfilled and 40 cancelled. The buyer, Seller and support team can explain the remaining collection or refund without charging the full order twice.

checks.journey: Operate recurring billing and stop it on cancellation
checks.normal_flow: Show the recurring agreement and next collection, notify the buyer of changes, and give a clear stop/cancellation result.
checks.exceptions: Cancellation near the next collection, failed collection, disputed consent, a changed price or recurring charges continuing after cancellation.
checks.issuing_handoff: The buyer's card activity distinguishes a prior valid charge from a later charge requiring correction; card replacement is not proof of renewed consent.
checks.account_control_handoff: Only authorized billing staff change an agreement; a helper cannot enroll someone without consent.
checks.etail_gap: Recurring mock schedules exist in product scope; consent, customer cancellation and post-cancellation service recovery are absent from the old merchant comparison rows.
checks.acceptance_scenario: Cancel before the next fictional billing date; no later collection starts. If a prior attempt was already completed, explain its status and assess any credit separately.

checks.journey: Submit sales and resolve late, duplicate or failed submissions
checks.normal_flow: Review which sales/credits were sent, distinguish accepted from unresolved items, and correct a submission through the responsible provider.
checks.exceptions: Late presentment, duplicate sales, amount/currency mismatch, one failed item in a batch or uncertain receipt of a file.
checks.issuing_handoff: The payer must not receive duplicate charges or an unexplained second charge used to repair a merchant submission error.
checks.account_control_handoff: A submitter can handle only its authorized locations; a payee's visibility does not automatically allow submission.
checks.etail_gap: Batch inspection exists in the catalog; explicit business handling of late, uncertain and partly failed submissions needs expansion.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A submitted batch is mistakenly sent again. Finance identifies the original sales and resolves the duplicate rather than treating the repeated batch as new revenue.

checks.journey: Understand pending and completed settlement
checks.normal_flow: Separate sales awaiting settlement from settled amounts and explain which sales and credits belong to each settlement.
checks.exceptions: Delayed provider confirmation, omitted sale, partial settlement or a completed checkout with no settlement yet.
checks.issuing_handoff: Cardholder payment history and merchant settlement are related but can reach their next stages at different times.
checks.account_control_handoff: Pending funds cannot be paid out or used as backing for Seller spending.
checks.etail_gap: The comparison covers stage visibility; the Seller still needs an understandable explanation of delays and next action.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A sale is approved but the settlement is pending. The Seller can find the sale and expected settlement while available funds and spending backing remain unchanged.

checks.journey: Explain fees, credits and other settlement deductions
checks.normal_flow: Show the amounts deducted or added, their reason, applicable price basis and the related sale or case where relevant.
checks.exceptions: Unrecognized fee, missing cost input, wrong plan, unexpected adjustment or deductions larger than current sales.
checks.issuing_handoff: A merchant fee does not appear as an unexplained buyer charge; a buyer credit is traceable separately.
checks.account_control_handoff: A bookkeeper can question a deduction without editing the balance or commercial pricing.
checks.etail_gap: Etail's Select/Premier economics remain normative; missing rate inputs and contested charges need a business resolution path.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A settlement includes an unexplained deduction. Finance opens a referenced question, sees its status and never sees an unknown fee represented as zero.

checks.journey: Understand and challenge a reserve or withholding
checks.normal_flow: Explain the withheld amount, business reason, affected funds, review route and any known release conditions; show later release or continued hold truthfully.
checks.exceptions: Unexpected increase, disputed reason, missed review date, reserve insufficient for an obligation or attempted withdrawal of held funds.
checks.issuing_handoff: A reserve is not a refund to a cardholder and does not remove an issuing obligation.
checks.account_control_handoff: Reserve administration and reserve release require appropriate authority; held funds cannot be pledged or paid out.
checks.etail_gap: Etail requires reserves, but reviewed public U.S. material does not establish a universal Amex reserve formula, notice, appeal or release schedule. Etail must specify its own mock policy.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A 100-dollar reserve remains held during a requested payout; the Seller can request review and see who must respond. No invented release date or cardholder credit is shown.

checks.journey: Resolve a merchant shortfall or negative balance
checks.normal_flow: Explain the shortfall, responsible party, permitted repayment or offset arrangement, and what remains restricted until resolved.
checks.exceptions: Refunds/chargebacks exceed receipts, insufficient bank funds, failed recovery, disputed debt or a shortfall after business closure.
checks.issuing_handoff: The buyer's legitimate credit and the merchant's recovery obligation are separate outcomes; do not delay explanation of one while collecting the other.
checks.account_control_handoff: No silent use of an unrelated Personal/Household account or another Seller's funds.
checks.etail_gap: The product names responsible merchant parties, but the precise recovery, notice and restriction policy for a merchant shortfall needs a business decision.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A Seller owes 30 dollars after refunds exceed receipts. Its own history shows the reason and allowed resolution; another Household member's funds are not taken.

checks.journey: Trace payout to the bank and resolve missing or returned funds
checks.normal_flow: Show the expected payout, submitted delivery and final bank-related outcome; help trace a missing deposit using the responsible party and reference.
checks.exceptions: Bank holiday/cutoff, wrong or closed destination, rejected or returned payment, partial delivery or Seller reporting no deposit.
checks.issuing_handoff: A merchant payout problem must not create another charge to the original cardholder.
checks.account_control_handoff: Only eligible available funds may be paid; a viewer cannot redirect delivery or reuse money already committed elsewhere.
checks.etail_gap: Amex paid-to-bank reporting is documented; bank confirmation, failure/return handling and promised timing are not fully covered by these public pages.
checks.acceptance_scenario: The provider shows paid but the Seller reports no deposit. Support opens a trace with the right funder; the app does not mark a second payout paid without resolving the first.

checks.journey: Change bank, contact or material business information
checks.normal_flow: Identify the exact account/location, verify authority, submit the proposed change and distinguish pending, failed and effective information.
checks.exceptions: Failed identity check, incorrect destination, change during an in-flight payout, changed legal ownership or disconnected alerts.
checks.issuing_handoff: A change to Seller details does not alter cardholder responsibility or unrelated issuing accounts.
checks.account_control_handoff: Financial destination, legal-party and notification changes have different authority and review needs.
checks.etail_gap: The current/effective change distinction is covered; ownership changes and the destination of in-flight payouts still require explicit business treatment.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A bank change is pending while a payout is already being delivered; the Seller is told which destination applies and a failed change does not silently replace the old one.

checks.journey: Refund all or part of an ordinary sale
checks.normal_flow: Locate the original sale, explain the requested credit and refundable remainder, submit an authorized full/partial refund and provide its progress to the buyer.
checks.exceptions: Repeated request, refund exceeds sale remainder, restricted Seller, insufficient eligible funds, failed credit or refund requested after a dispute began.
checks.issuing_handoff: The cardholder can distinguish a refund requested, pending and posted; spending/rewards adjustments follow the actual credit outcome.
checks.account_control_handoff: Refund authority is separate from viewing payments; the original merchant scope stays intact.
checks.etail_gap: The product specifies refunds, but a standalone refund journey is not a distinct old merchant comparison row. Exact timing, funding and recovery choices need a business specification.
checks.acceptance_scenario: After a 100-dollar sale and 30-dollar refund, a second 80-dollar request is not silently paid. Staff see the 70-dollar remainder and explain the available resolution.

checks.journey: Receive an inquiry and gather the right response
checks.normal_flow: Identify the challenged sale, reason, amount, required reply and deadline owner; gather the specific evidence and respond through the correct service route.
checks.exceptions: Payer does not recognize the seller, wrong location, missing documents, overlapping merchant/issuer conversations or no assigned responder.
checks.issuing_handoff: The issuer's initial cardholder question may be resolved before merchant contact; merchant response is not automatic case success.
checks.account_control_handoff: Only the relevant Seller/location responder can see the case and its buyer information.
checks.etail_gap: Existing dispute rows need an explicit cross-party owner and next-response explanation.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An inquiry reaches a multi-location Seller. The correct responder sees the requested information and reply-by source; another location's viewer cannot answer it.

checks.journey: Handle an upfront chargeback and decide whether to contest
checks.normal_flow: Tell the Seller whether money has already been taken, what evidence is requested and whether contesting remains available.
checks.exceptions: Chargeback arrives before a merchant inquiry, disputed amount differs from sale, late notice or Seller cannot support its position.
checks.issuing_handoff: A chargeback response and a later cardholder outcome must not be confused with a new merchant refund.
checks.account_control_handoff: Case-response permission does not grant payout or bank-setting authority.
checks.etail_gap: The underlying case types are covered; the debited amount and dispute work need a joint business walkthrough.
checks.acceptance_scenario: An upfront 20-dollar chargeback arrives on a 100-dollar sale. The Seller sees 20 debited and an open response opportunity without the entire sale becoming refunded.

checks.journey: Submit evidence and handle rejected, late or insufficient replies
checks.normal_flow: Prepare relevant documents/explanation, submit before the displayed deadline and show whether the response and documents were accepted for review.
checks.exceptions: Unreadable attachment, rejected format, document-processing failure, insufficient reply, missed deadline or one failed case in a bulk response.
checks.issuing_handoff: An uploaded file is not proof the issuer received usable evidence or reversed the buyer's credit.
checks.account_control_handoff: Evidence and bulk actions remain limited to authorized cases; removal of access transfers work to another responder.
checks.etail_gap: Failure handling is in the catalog; distinguish merchant preparation, provider receipt and review in customer language.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A response is sent but its evidence fails processing before the deadline; staff see the actionable failure and repair it without submitting a second financial resolution.

checks.journey: Resolve a claim with a prior or partial refund
checks.normal_flow: Review existing credits/debits before agreeing, contesting or offering a permitted partial resolution; explain which route will return any remaining amount.
checks.exceptions: A refund and chargeback overlap, credit is still pending, only part of the claim is accepted or the case type disallows the offered option.
checks.issuing_handoff: The buyer receives the supported total resolution once; the Seller can explain prior credit versus new money.
checks.account_control_handoff: Case responders cannot silently exceed their refund approval authority.
checks.etail_gap: The prior-refund safeguard is covered; partial-resolution options need precise case eligibility and buyer communication.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A 100-dollar dispute overlaps a 40-dollar pending refund. Staff first account for the existing credit and cannot promise another 100 dollars as an automatic outcome.

checks.journey: Close a dispute and verify the resulting money
checks.normal_flow: Record the case result, explain its business meaning and reconcile any debit, reversal or credit before treating the financial question as finished.
checks.exceptions: Case closed while an adjustment is missing, loss after a promised refund, partial win, reopened question or unfamiliar outcome wording.
checks.issuing_handoff: Merchant case result and the cardholder's final bill/credit must be explainable without exposing private issuer information.
checks.account_control_handoff: Closing a case does not grant authority to alter an account balance.
checks.etail_gap: Closed-case history exists in the benchmark; final money confirmation and any reopened customer question remain separate checks.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A case is won but no reversal is visible. The case records the win while finance has an open money-tracing task; available funds do not increase on the label alone.

checks.journey: Reconcile a period and produce useful statements/reports
checks.normal_flow: Compare sales, credits, deductions, settlement and bank receipts for a chosen period/currency/location; save and retrieve the needed statement or report.
checks.exceptions: Unmatched sale/deposit, timing boundary, revised filters, late adjustment, unavailable period, failed report or revoked report access.
checks.issuing_handoff: Merchant reports must not reveal the cardholder's other purchases or private issuing-account data.
checks.account_control_handoff: Report/export scope follows current grants; a saved report is not permanent access to a removed location.
checks.etail_gap: Existing rows cover report actions; a complete business reconciliation needs an explicit unresolved-difference owner and period explanation.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A refund posts after the sale's statement period. The next report explains the timing difference and both periods remain traceable without rewriting the older statement.

checks.journey: Restrict or close merchant activity while finishing obligations
checks.normal_flow: Explain which new activity stops, what remains open, how outstanding orders/refunds/disputes are serviced and when closure is complete.
checks.exceptions: Unfulfilled advance payment, recurring agreement, pending bank change, reserve, unresolved payout/refund/dispute or later chargeback.
checks.issuing_handoff: Stopping merchant acceptance does not erase the buyer's service/credit rights or the Seller's separate issuing debt.
checks.account_control_handoff: History and necessary servicing remain available only to authorized people after new-money activity stops.
checks.etail_gap: Etail specifies closure prerequisites, but a complete merchant exit/appeal and post-closure servicing policy is not established by the public U.S. pages reviewed.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A Seller requests closure with an open refund and dispute. New collection stops as policy permits; the outstanding work has named owners and closure is not falsely complete.

checks.journey: Get help, escalate a complaint and retain responsibility
checks.normal_flow: Start help from the relevant payment/case/change, receive a reference and next step, and escalate a complaint without losing the original issue.
checks.exceptions: Wrong service organization, closed support hours, missed response, dispute deadline approaching or unresolved complaint after account closure.
checks.issuing_handoff: A buyer's charge dispute and a Seller's service complaint can coexist; neither automatically closes the other.
checks.account_control_handoff: Staff share only needed case information; the complaint follows the affected business, not everyone using the login.
checks.etail_gap: Public routes exist, but U.S. merchant complaint categories, escalation stages and promised resolution times remain unverified. Define Etail's service policy.
checks.acceptance_scenario: A missing-payout complaint is raised with the wrong provider; it receives a reference, responsible funder and next action while any dispute deadline remains visible.
